title: Longest Stretch With Capped Repeats
statement:
You get an integer array nums and an integer k. A contiguous subarray is capped if no value appears in it more than k times.

Return the length of the longest capped subarray.

examples.why: The whole array has three 3s. Dropping the first element leaves [1, 3, 2, 3, 1, 2], where every value appears exactly twice.
No value reaches 4, so the whole array is capped.

hints: If a subarray is capped, so is every subarray inside it. That monotonic property suggests a window.
Grow the window to the right one element at a time, keeping a count of each value inside.
When the new element's count goes above k, move the left edge right, decrementing counts, until that value is back to k. Record the window length after each step.

explain.intuition:
Capped subarrays are closed under shrinking: removing elements can only lower counts. So for each right end, the valid left ends form a suffix, and the best one is the furthest left that still works. As the right end moves right, that best left end never moves back. That is exactly a sliding window.

Only the value just added can break the rule, so after adding nums[right] you shrink until count[nums[right]] ≤ k. It works like a rate limiter that drops the oldest events once one key gets too many.
steps: While count[nums[right]] > k, decrement count[nums[left]] and move left right.
Update best = max(best, right − left + 1). Return best at the end.
pitfalls: Checking every value's count after each step. Only the value just added can exceed k.
Shrinking until the window is fully distinct instead of until the one offending value is at k.
Jumping left straight past the first occurrence of the value, which only works for k = 1.

solutions.title: Every start, extend until it breaks
solutions.idea: For each left end, extend right with fresh counts until some value exceeds k.

solutions.title: Sliding window with counts
solutions.idea: Grow the right edge; when the new value exceeds k, shrink from the left until it does not.

followups: Each value has its own cap. What changes?
Count how many subarrays are capped instead of finding the longest.
